title: Reconstruct Word2Vec
summary: Recover the distributional objective behind Skip-gram, then implement stable softmax and the full-softmax training loss.

parts.title: Distributional meaning
parts.prompt: Why can predicting nearby words produce semantic vector structure without explicit labels?
parts.answer: Words used in similar contexts receive similar gradient updates. The prediction objective therefore organizes embeddings by distributional similarity, allowing semantic and syntactic relationships to emerge.
hints: What training signal is available in raw text?

parts.title: Skip-gram direction
parts.prompt: In Skip-gram, what is the input and what is predicted for each training pair?
parts.answer: The center word selects an input embedding, and the model predicts a surrounding context word through scores against output embeddings.
hints: One center can produce several training pairs.

parts.title: Why negative sampling?
parts.prompt: Why is full-vocabulary softmax expensive, and how does negative sampling change the task?
parts.answer: Full softmax scores every vocabulary item for every pair. Negative sampling replaces multiclass normalization with a few binary decisions: distinguish the observed pair from sampled noise words.
hints: Count output dot products per example.
The approximation changes the training objective.

parts.title: Implement stable softmax
parts.prompt: Convert a vector of logits into probabilities without overflow.

parts.title: Implement Skip-gram loss
parts.prompt: Use the center embedding and all output embeddings to compute full-softmax cross-entropy for one context target.
